claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a high-temperature disordered BCC state.
Diffusion-driven short-range ordering during cooling or thermal exposure causes elemental partitioning in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Elemental partitioning triggers localized nucleation of secondary phases from the disordered BCC matrix.
The secondary phases produced by the proposed mechanism may include B2 or FCC domains.
Slow cooling or extended moderate-temperature aging provides sufficient atomic mobility for diffusion and ordering.
Rapid quenching freezes the disordered state by suppressing diffusion.
Temperatures below a diffusion threshold suppress appreciable ordering and secondary-phase formation.
Local compositional fluctuations include short-range ordering or clustering of Ni and Al.
Ni-Al clustering and related compositional fluctuations lower local free energy and stabilize secondary phases.
Limited diffusion during cooling or aging produces subtle elemental partitioning within the BCC matrix.
Partitioned regions provide lower-free-energy sites at which B2 or FCC domains can nucleate.
Competition between thermodynamic driving forces and kinetic limitations leads to multiphase coexistence over time.
A rapidly quenched baseline is expected to remain single-phase BCC with negligible elemental segregation.
Relative to the quenched baseline, slowly cooled or aged samples will develop new diffraction peaks from secondary phases.
Relative to the quenched baseline, slowly cooled or aged samples will show TEM or atom-probe signatures of secondary phases and local ordering.
Comparable secondary-phase formation in quenched and slowly cooled or aged samples would falsify the proposed diffusion-controlled ordering mechanism.
An absence of differences in phase distribution or ordering between rapid- and slow-cooling treatments would falsify the proposed mechanism.
